claims.text: A hybrid method coupling an ML interatomic potential with enhanced-sampling free-energy pathway integration can reproduce phase free energies at fusion temperatures.
The phase free energies reproduced by the method retain vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration effects.
The hybrid method costs substantially less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
The proposed performance and cost advantages extend to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The ML potential will be trained on a curated ab initio dataset and combined with enhanced sampling for free-energy pathway integration.
Periodic recalibration against ab initio benchmarks is part of the proposed method.
The method is intended to operate from approximately 0.6 to 1.2 times the melting temperature and cover both solid and liquid phases.
The ML interatomic potential can encapsulate vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration coupling characteristics.
A limited, judiciously selected training dataset can accurately learn the relevant ab initio free-energy landscape.
The learned ML potential enables rapid trajectory generation under enhanced sampling.
Periodic ab initio recalibration minimizes errors in vibrational and anharmonic free-energy contributions.
The method should predict phase free energies within approximately 10 meV/atom of explicit ab initio MD results.
The method should predict melting temperatures within approximately 50 K of explicit ab initio MD results.
The method should significantly reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio MD.
The method should mitigate TOR-TILD scaling problems in multicomponent systems.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows are computationally expensive.
TOR-TILD scales poorly for complex alloy systems.
Applicability is expected to extend from elemental and binary systems to high-entropy alloys.
